The Map
The federal maps shade the West Side red. The banks won't lend here, the insurers won't write here, and the only way to buy a house is on contract. Families start reading their contracts together.

REDLINING is active from round 1, and from round 2, while it stays active, the map compounds: it tightens a second time every round (+1 Squeeze on the weaker of Housing and Lending). Break it, or it breaks you.
The Appraiser
The Appraiser: leans on your strongest unfinished district every round (+1 Squeeze); on reveal, knocks one woken district back to Clarity 1.
The League

Like the Contract Buyers League (Chicago, 1968): sign the pledge to withhold together (an action). Every family must sign in the same round, or the sellers scare them off and the pledges fall apart. Once it forms: Housing Squeeze −2 at once, Housing −1 every second round after, and every Housing and Lending trap can be negotiated with Read 1.
Stay and fight for the house, or move to where the map says you can?
Stay and fight
Housing keeps its stickers, and the family's Ledger +1: they held the line.
Move
Remove one Scar from Housing, but the Elder stays behind: in Chapter 4 the Elder starts with no Read and no History.
Freedom's Ledger

The family is newly free. They save what they can, learn to read by lamplight, raise a church and a school, and sign the only contracts on offer: the crop lien, the store's book, the year-long labor contract.
Nobody starts with Read, not even the Elder: the family learns everything at the table. And the crop lien grips from the first day: Lending starts at Squeeze 2.
The Planter's Ledger
The Planter's Ledger: every shortcut costs +1 extra Shady, and each round the store calls in its book: anyone carrying Shady loses 1 Trust. The Fallen strike twice as hard.
Go north now, or stay one more season and save?
Go north now
Chapter 2 starts with all five districts open from round 1.
Stay and save
The family's Ledger +1, but Chapter 2 starts with Lending at Squeeze 1 (the debt follows you).
Up North
The family steps off the train on Dayton's West Side with a labor agent's ticket and a room they haven't seen. The plants are hiring. The fine print came north too.
Only Lending, Housing and Labor are open at first. Health and Education open in round 3, once the family is settled.
The Labor Agent
The Labor Agent: every round it leans on your strongest unfinished district (+1 Squeeze); on reveal, knocks one woken district back to Clarity 1.
The family has a little saved. Put it into the church, the house, or a child's schooling?
The church
In Chapter 3, gathering at the church takes off 3 Shady instead of 2.
The house
In Chapter 3, Housing starts with 1 less Squeeze: a house the family owns outright.
A child's schooling
In Chapter 3, the Student starts with Read 1 everywhere.
Voice
Boycotts in Montgomery, a strike in Memphis, and on the West Side the family is registering voters. In 1970 Dayton elects James H. McGee mayor. Somebody keeps offering the organizers a quieter way.
The Organizer's NEGOTIATE clears 3 Squeeze. Once per game, any player can call the March (an action): every player gathers at once (Trust +2, Shady −1, covered).
The Council
The Council: leans on your strongest unfinished district every round (+1 Squeeze); on reveal, it redraws the lines: every woken district loses 1 Clarity.
Run for office, or keep organizing?
Run for office
In Chapter 5, the Owner's hidden hand rests for the first 3 rounds.
Keep organizing
In Chapter 5, the Organizer starts with 5 Trust.
GM's Moraine plant closes in 2008; NCR leaves in 2009. Before the crash, the brokers came door to door with teaser rates and cash-out refinances. Now the temp agency is the only one hiring.

Labor starts at Squeeze 2 and everyone starts with 1 Trust. Before the chapter the family chooses: defend what you built (the Machine strikes your Rebuilt districts first) or let one go (remove one Rebuilt sticker).
The Algorithm: scoring, automation and risk models. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.
Sell the house at the bottom of the market, or hold on?
Sell
In Chapter 6, everyone starts with +2 Trust, but Housing loses a Rebuilt sticker.
Hold on
Housing keeps everything, and starts Chapter 6 with 1 more Squeeze.
Today
Good Samaritan Hospital has closed. Gem City Market has opened. The family is still here, and the trap is still here, wearing new clothes.
Every History card the family unlocked is in play, and the Elder may teach History twice.
The Ledger Keeper

The Ledger Keeper: one hand behind every era. Its hidden hand changes face each round: the store's book (collections), the labor agent (Read −1), the appraiser (+1 Squeeze on your strongest work), the algorithm (an extra strike). It wore The Planter's Ledger, the Labor Agent, the Appraiser, the Council and the Algorithm.
The Chain
Graduation night
Marcus can see the second number on everything now, and he teaches it as fast as he can: to Nia, who teaches the next one, who teaches the next.
A Block Party with the Terrell rule. The Chain: when a learner says the second number back, they at once teach one more player in that district, for free.
No Owner
If anyone was burned by the Terrell rule, the ledger reads Terrell. If you won, the block learns Civic Armor: from Chapter 2 on, every Teach comes with cover.
The Net
A county job
A county job, a desk, a program that sounds like help. The terms keep changing on you.

Full Block with fine-print dice. The Desk: at the start of round 2 one player may take the Desk. At the Desk they gain +1 Trust every round but can't face deals or teach, and every second round its paperwork feeds the Machine an extra strike. Leaving it, for good, takes an action.
The Net: the program that sounds like help. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.
If the player at the Desk left it, the ledger reads Quit the desk: in Chapter 3 that player starts with Read 1 everywhere.
The Crown
A way up
Somebody offers Dre a way up out of the life, and it looks just like a blessing.

Overlord mode, with the stranger's handwriting in place of the Terrell rule. The Crown: once per game the Overlord may offer the Crown to one player. A crowned player can't Fall, but every other block player loses 1 Trust at the start of each round. Refuse it, and the Overlord takes one extra move that round.
The Overlord
The ledger records whether anyone wore the Crown.
The Empty Throne
No neck for a crown
No card table to shut down. No leader to arrest. The only way to win is for everybody to read.
Full Block with endless deals. No neck for a crown: you can't Expose the Owner until every player has taught at least once, and while any one player holds more than half the table's Props.
The Empty Throne: no face at all, just the system. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.
The book's last scene is on a porch. If you won, read it aloud.
The Long Ledger
One West Dayton family across six generations, from Reconstruction to today.
Book One
Four chapters that follow the novel, from graduation night to the empty throne.
